[GitLab Singapore Pte Ltd > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves]
GitLab Singapore combines statutory leave with our global parental leave policy to provide comprehensive support for growing families.

Team members employed for at least 3 months before birth may be eligible for the maternity leaves listed below.

Government-Paid Maternity Leave (16 weeks)

- **1st and 2nd births**: 8 weeks employer-paid + 8 weeks government-paid
- **3rd+ births**: 16 weeks government-paid
- First 8 weeks must be continuous; remaining weeks flexible within 12 months of birth
- Eligible team members receive concurrent [GitLab Parental Leave](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave)

Employment Act Maternity Leave (12 weeks)

- 8 weeks paid + 4 weeks unpaid
- With [GitLab Parental Leave](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave), eligible team members receive up to 16 weeks paid

How to Apply

1. Submit "Parental Leave" request in Workday at least 30 days before leave
2. Send [GPML Declaration Form](https://file.go.gov.sg/gpml1form.pdf) to leaves@gitlab.com
3. GitLab handles government reimbursement claims

[GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family leaves > Maternity Leave]
Leave Entitlement

- Team members must have continuous employment with GitLab for at least 26 weeks leading up to the "qualifying week" (15th week before the expected week of childbirth)
- Up to 52 weeks leave available
- First 39 weeks paid (combining statutory and GitLab benefits)
- 90% of average earnings for first 6 weeks (before tax), then statutory rate (£194.32/week) or 90% (whichever is lower) of the team member's average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks. This also applies to the leave amounts provided for Parental Leave and Adoption Leave.
- GitLab's enhanced policy provides up to 16 weeks at 100% salary

How to Apply

[Global Expansion > **Global Expansion Benefits** > Denmark 🇩🇰]
**Maternity and Paternity Leave Payment**
The maximum maternity and paternity leave payment in Denmark is **DKK 4,865 per week (2025)** for full-time employees working 37 hours per week.

- If you are employed full-time and earn more than DKK 21,092 per month, you will receive the maximum weekly benefit of DKK 4,865 before tax.
- Maternity and paternity benefits are calculated based on your hourly wage (excluding Labour Market Contribution) and the number of hours of leave taken per week.
- In 2025, the maximum hourly rate for maternity benefits is DKK 131.49 per hour (4,865 ÷ 37 hours). If your hourly wage is lower than this, benefits will be paid at your usual hourly rate.
- Employees with a permanent job in addition to their education can apply for maternity benefits as a salaried employee for the hours during which they work.

If eligible, [GitLab's Parental leave](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/leave-types/#gitlab-parental-leave) will be applied concurrently with the statutory leave and/or pay entitlements the team member is eligible for. GitLab will top up state maternity/paternity benefits to ensure you receive 100% of your salary for up to 16 weeks (*). Any additional leave taken (up to 52 weeks total) will be unpaid by GitLab and paid at the statutory rate only.

*GX (GitLab’s employer of record) will seek reimbursement from the public authority; Udbetaling Danmark for the state funded portion.
